countries/nepal.summary: Catastrophic flash flooding struck Nepal (and the Tibet/China border region) beginning 2026-08-26; the death toll in Nepal crossed 1,000 by 2026-09-01 with nearly 4,000 people reported missing and rescue operations ongoing. CNN reported that 'warning signs were visible ahead of' the flooding, raising a state protective-failure question about early-warning systems. Displaced residents are in inadequate temporary shelter (e.g. ~100 women and children sharing one bathroom at a Bidur shelter; one 250-household community swept away entirely). This is a materially firmer, better-dated version of a story the 2026-09-01 scan carried only as unattributed cross-country context in sector_alerts ('did not attribute the death toll cleanly to a single dated, sourceable incident per country'); this cycle resolves that gap with country-specific, dated, multiply-sourced reporting for Nepal.

countries/democratic-republic-of-c.summary: WHO declared the end of the DRC's 2026 Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) epidemic on 2026-08-25 after 42 days without a new confirmed case; a 2026-09-02 case-count update put the final cumulative toll at 6,250 confirmed cases and 3,039 deaths, making it the largest and fastest-growing Ebola outbreak ever recorded in the country (PHEIC declared 2026-05-17; expanded to 54 health zones across six provinces). Distinct from the eastern-DRC conflict evidence (dated 2026-08-21) that this entity was already assessed against on 2026-09-01 (last_assessed=2026-09-01 per rotation-state) -- this is new information about the health-system/outbreak-response track, not a reproduction of the prior assessment's evidence.

fortune-500/boeing.summary: The FAA disclosed to Reuters on 2026-09-02 (previously undisclosed to the public) that Boeing paid the full $3,139,319 civil penalty proposed in September 2025 for a series of safety violations tied to the 2024 Alaska Airlines MAX 9 mid-air door-plug emergency, including presenting two aircraft for certification that were not airworthy and interfering with the independence of company safety officials. Boeing quietly paid the fine in January 2026. The underlying conduct is not new (already within the benchmark's historical record), but the public disclosure -- and its five-plus-month delay -- is new and relevant to transparency/governance scoring; last_assessed 2026-06-10 predates this disclosure.
